items.description: Authorities work to rescue 5 surviving whales in poor health
items.author: Berk Kutay Gokmen
items.excerpt: Nineteen sperm whales died Thursday after becoming stranded on Ninety Mile Beach in northern New Zealand. Five others were in poor health as rescuers and Indigenous communities responded to the stranding. The whales came ashore at the northern end of the beach, also known as Te Oneroa-a-Tohe, according to Radio New Zealand (RNZ). New Zealand’s Department of Conservation (DOC) said it was working alongside local Maori tribes and that the surviving whales remained in poor health. “The situation remains dynamic, and assessments are ongoing,” said Laree Furniss, DOC operations manager in Kaitaia.
